newFindings.title: Material refresh incorrectly equated current revisions with episode-entry and lock-adoption revisions
newFindings.problem: observeHorizonEpisodes preserves entry metadata while ordinal is unchanged, and advanceLock preserves adoption metadata when start is unchanged. Strict equality with current opportunity revisions rejected valid material updates.
newFindings.reproduction: Keep horizon and start unchanged; revise schedule or affiliation; feed helper-produced episode and lock plus new opportunity to runPreparedIssuance. Initial reviewed source returned prepared_identity_episode_or_lock_mismatch.
newFindings.repairObserved: Lead replaced equality with nonempty historical lineage validation at lines 72–73 during review. Source rechecked; regression execution remains lead-owned.

newFindings.title: Fresh history requests cannot reach games removed from active player context
newFindings.problem: history without a cursor reads only the latest player context and then searches its at-most-ten games. After an old completed/cancelled target leaves that queue, initial history becomes unavailable even though immutable history remains. Only callers preserving an old context cursor can still reach it.
newFindings.reproduction: Persist context A containing game G and vintages; then context B with the current next ten excluding G. Call history(player,G,profile) without cursor: context B yields no game and returns null.
newFindings.repair: Provide a bounded game-specific context lookup independent of active player queue; test a new reader starting old/cancelled/postgame history.
newFindings.repairObserved: PostgresContextReader.readGame now selects latest retained context containing the requested game; history uses readGame while retaining cursor context identity. Bounded source reinspection completed; lead owns native/API regression execution.

finding.title: Lock successor can reuse its predecessor scientific ID
finding.problem: Snapshot hashes distinguish bytes but lock validation permits value.id===predecessor.id and value.predecessorId===predecessor.id, producing two conflicting LockEpoch payloads with one scientific ID. Evaluation resolves epoch IDs directly.
finding.requestedRepair: Require distinct scientific ID for lock successors; preserve the deliberate episode closure exception.
finding.repairObserved: Lock and event branches explicitly reject successor scientific ID equal to predecessor ID; episode closure remains the deliberate same-ID exception.
